claim: The S3 bucket policy for OAC allows the CloudFront service principal (cloudfront.amazonaws.com) to access the bucket, and a Condition element limits it to requests on behalf of the distribution that contains the S3 origin.
question: Which principal does the S3 bucket policy for CloudFront OAC name?

values.display: only when the request is on behalf

evidence.quote: Use an S3 [bucket policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-policies.html) to allow the CloudFront service principal (`cloudfront.amazonaws.com`) to access the bucket. Use a `Condition` element in the policy to allow CloudFront to access the bucket only when the request is on behalf of the CloudFront distribution that contains the S3 origin.

claim: A default root object is the object CloudFront requests from the origin when a viewer asks for the root URL, and specifying one avoids exposing the contents of your distribution.
question: What does a CloudFront default root object do?

values.display: Specifying a default root object avoids exposing
viewer requests the root URL of your distribution

evidence.quote: Optional. The object that you want CloudFront to request from your origin (for example, `index.html`) when a viewer requests the root URL of your distribution (`https://www.example.com/`) instead of an object in your distribution (`https://www.example.com/product-description.html`). Specifying a default root object avoids exposing the contents of your distribution.

claim: By default, CloudFront serves your objects from edge locations in all CloudFront Regions; a price class corresponds to the maximum price you want to pay.
question: Which edge locations does a CloudFront distribution use by default?

values.display: By default, CloudFront serves your objects from edge

evidence.quote: Choose the price class that corresponds with the maximum price that you want to pay for CloudFront service. By default, CloudFront serves your objects from edge locations in all CloudFront Regions.

claim: Selecting Enable IPv6 makes CloudFront respond to viewer requests from both IPv4 and IPv6 IP addresses.
question: How does a distribution answer viewers that use IPv6?

values.display: respond to viewer requests from IPv4 and IPv6 IP addresses

evidence.quote: If you want CloudFront to respond to viewer requests from IPv4 and IPv6 IP addresses, select **Enable IPv6**.

claim: CloudFront edge locations provide automatic, always-on mitigation of network and transport layer (Layer 3 and 4) attacks, protecting both the CDN service and your origin.
question: What DDoS mitigation does CloudFront provide automatically at the edge?

values.display: automatic, always-on mitigation of network and transport layer

evidence.quote: CloudFront edge locations provide automatic, always-on mitigation of network and transport layer (Layer 3 and 4) attacks, protecting both the CDN service and your origin infrastructure.

claim: CloudFront automatically closes connections from slow reading or slow writing attackers such as Slowloris, and from novel attacks such as HTTP/2 rapid reset.
question: Which slow-connection attacks does CloudFront close automatically?

values.display: automatically closes connections from slow reading or slow

evidence.quote: CloudFront automatically closes connections from slow reading or slow writing attackers (for example, [Slowloris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slowloris_(computer_security))), or novel attacks such as HTTP/2 rapid reset.

claim: AWS WAF capacity on CloudFront is scaled to match the capacity of the CloudFront points of presence, so the capacity constraints of Regional WAF do not apply.
question: How does AWS WAF capacity on CloudFront compare with Regional WAF?

values.display: scaled to match the CloudFront points of presence
the capacity constraints of Regional WAF don't apply

evidence.quote: CloudFront WAF capacity is scaled to match the CloudFront points of presence (POP) capacity—the capacity constraints of Regional WAF don't apply.

claim: The CloudFront cache hierarchy of edge POPs, regional edge caches and Origin Shield, together with request collapsing, keeps most requests, even during request floods, from reaching the origin.
question: How does CloudFront caching protect an origin during a request flood?

values.display: consolidating multiple simultaneous requests into a single origin

evidence.quote: For content that isn't yet cached or has expired, CloudFront [request collapsing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/RequestAndResponseBehaviorCustomOrigin.html#request-custom-traffic-spikes) further protects origins by consolidating multiple simultaneous requests into a single origin request.
